clauses.reason: Terminated by express supersession. EO 8384 (Franklin D. Roosevelt, signed March 29, 1940), section 21: "This order shall supersede" the earlier orders, including "8226 of August 24, 1939", and it is "effective as of March 2, 1940". The held text names EO 8226 with its number and date. The end is recorded at the stated effective date March 2, 1940, which precedes the signing date; the signing date is the alternative reading. EO 8384 section 15 restates the same temporary-employee leave rule, so the rule continues under the later order.

conflict_resolutions.EVENT_BEFORE_SIGNING: The flagged supersession is EO 7845 of March 21, 1938, the order whose section 15 EO 8226 (August 24, 1939) amends. It is the target of the amendment and an earlier order, not a later event that could end EO 8226; the end recorded here is EO 8384 section 21 (held Federal Register text).

research_rationale:
EO 8226 (August 24, 1939, Franklin D. Roosevelt), read in full in the held Federal Register text, amends section 15 of EO 7845 of March 21, 1938 (annual leave regulations) to read as follows (a rule that temporary employees who "subsequently receive indefinite," emergency, probational or permanent appointments without a break in service are entitled to stated annual leave), and the order is effective as of June 30, 1939. EO 8384 (March 29, 1940; 5 FR 1253, issue of Tuesday, April 2, 1940) prescribes new annual leave regulations and, in its section 21, states "This order shall supersede" EO 7845, EO 7879 and EO 8226 and the order is "effective as of March 2, 1940", except as to its own sections 6 and 9. EO 8226 has no term of its own, so the first end is that express supersession.

The effective-as-of wording in EO 8384 section 21 reaches back before the signing date (March 29, 1940) to March 2, 1940, and the claim records March 2, 1940 as the effective date of the supersession as the order's own words state; March 29, 1940 is the alternative reading for a reviewer who treats the retroactive date as not governing.","independent_command_check":"No independent command survives. savings.reason: The substance of EO 8226 continues in the superseding order: section 15 of EO 8384 carries the same rule that temporary employees who "subsequently receive indefinite," emergency, probational or permanent appointments in the same department or agency without a break in service are entitled to annual leave for each full month and are credited with accrued leave. Leave earned under EO 8226 between June 30, 1939 and March 2, 1940 is an accrued effect; the held EO 8384 text provides for adjustment of leave on the basis of its regulations in section 21 and no held source shows any loss of leave earned under EO 8226.
